newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo corn futures plunge, all months limit-down.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo corn futures plunge, all months limit-down.

text.p: Tokyo corn futures plunged on Wednesday, with all contracts down by their daily limits of 400 yen, as the yen's firmer tone against the dollar and the Chicago market's price falls triggered heavy selling orders, traders said.
Benchmark July 1998 contract was down 400 yen at 12,950 yen per tonne. Volume was estimated at 80,739 lots.

All contracts fell from the opening session, as local investors actively liquidated long positions, traders said. "Individual investors accelerated their selling by early afternoon," a brokerage house trader said.
The spot July corn contract on the CBOT Project A overnight trading system stood at $2.42-3/4 per bushel at 0825 GMT, down from $2.43-1/4 at Tuesday's close.
Spot July CBOT soybean futures were trading at $7.34-1/2 a bushel at 0825 GMT, against $7.32 at Tuesday's close.
